name: Reputify.io – Review Widgets, Score and Review Requests
author: SERVIT Software Solutions

sections.description:
Reputify collects your reviews from Google, Trustpilot, Facebook, ProvenExpert, Trusted Shops, Booking.com, Airbnb, Tripadvisor, Etsy and Herold in one place and calculates the Reputify Score. This plugin is the WordPress side of the Reputify service: it shows your reviews on your website and transfers WooCommerce orders for review requests. It needs a Reputify account – the free plan stays free for good, and the plugin never stops working after a trial period.

Six blocks

  • Score badge – compact seal with the Reputify Score, linked to your Reputify profile.
  • Review widget – average, count and the latest reviews as a list.
  • Carousel – reviews as a running row.
  • Single review – one selected review as a quote, for landing pages.
  • Video review – video with transcript, loaded only after a click.
  • Certificate – your awarded distinction with year and a link to check it.

All blocks are in the editor under the Reputify category. For the Classic Editor, Elementor, WPBakery, Divi and themes without block support there are shortcodes, and a widget for sidebars and footers. Where the reviews come from is chosen per block: the whole account, one location or one review group.

A builder instead of a shortcode reference

Under Reputify → Blocks you choose a block and its options and read off the finished shortcode and the finished block code, with a live preview of the real block next to them. Only the options that block actually has are offered, so nothing is mistyped and nothing is forgotten.

On every page

A top bar above the navigation, a footer bar at the very bottom and a tab at the edge of the screen that opens the reviews over the page. Switched on in the settings, with a drawing of where each one sits; the bars can stay fixed while scrolling, and look, source and number are set per placement.

Set up in two steps

Check the e-mail address, agree – the Reputify account is created without leaving WordPress. Then choose your platform and connect it in Reputify, already signed in; afterwards you are back in WordPress and see your reviews being fetched. Already have an account? Connect it in the Reputify window. No API key to copy, none stored.

Text on your page, not in a frame

Review blocks are rendered on your server into the page itself – search engines read them as part of your content. Seals are plain images with a link and work without JavaScript.

WooCommerce review requests

Completed orders are transferred to a review survey in your Reputify account; Reputify does the sending, the reminders and the unsubscribe link. The plugin decides which orders are transferred: only with the consent checkbox ticked at checkout (never pre-ticked, never required), not after a refund, optionally not below a minimum basket value. Off by default.

Privacy

No cookies, no tracking of your visitors. Delivered from the EU, hosted in Austria and Germany.

External services

This plugin is an interface to the Reputify service (https://reputify.io), operated by Reputify. It connects to it as follows:

  • app.reputify.io – only after you click a button on the setup page:
    • “Create account and connect”: registers this website as an application and creates a Reputify account. Transferred: the e-mail address you entered and the address and name of this website. Nothing is sent before you agreed to the terms and conditions and the terms of use on that screen.
    • “I already have a Reputify account”: opens the Reputify consent dialog; afterwards access is issued and renewed.
    • “Open in Reputify” and “Connect Google now”: the plugin asks Reputify for a one-time sign-in link (valid two minutes, usable once) and opens it in a new tab, so you land in your project signed in. Nothing is sent besides the requested page.
  • api.reputify.io/v1/platform-types – on the setup page: the list of supported platforms with name and icon (public, no account data is sent). The icons are loaded from app.reputify.io.
  • api.reputify.io/v1/industries – on the setup and settings pages: the list of industries with the word widgets use for reviewers (public, no account data is sent). The chosen industry is sent with the account creation, or when you change it in the settings.
  • api.reputify.io – from the WordPress admin, the block editor and the twice-daily background job: the block catalogue, the figures of your project, setting up embeds for this website and – only with WooCommerce review requests switched on – transferring orders (order number, customer name, e-mail address, purchased products) and fetching their status.
  • cdn.reputify.io – rendering the blocks. Review blocks are fetched by your server and cached; seals and frame blocks (tab, streams, video players, location picker) are loaded by your visitors’ browsers from this host. No cookies are set.

Terms and conditions: https://reputify.io/terms · Terms of use: https://reputify.io/terms-of-use · Privacy policy: https://reputify.io/privacy
sections.installation:
1. Install and activate the plugin.
  2. Go to Reputify → Setup, choose your platform and create your account – or connect an existing one.
  3. Add a block from the Reputify category, a shortcode, or the “Reputify reviews” widget.
sections.faq:
Do I need a Reputify account?

Yes – the plugin shows what your Reputify project contains. It is created on the setup screen; the free plan is enough to start.

Do I have to paste an API key?

No.

Will my site get slower?

No. Blocks are cached on your server and revalidated in the background; seals have a fixed size, so nothing jumps while loading.

Which shortcodes are there?

[reputify_badge], [reputify_widget], [reputify_carousel], [reputify_review id="…"], [reputify_video], [reputify_certificate]. Attributes: form (another form of the block), loc or group (source), reviews (number), min_rating (from stars), product (SKU or auto), theme (light, dark, auto), locale (de, en).

Are review requests by e-mail allowed?

They count as advertising in parts of the EU. That is why the transfer is off by default and only orders with the consent checkbox ticked are transferred. Whether you may send them is up to you as the shop owner.
sections.changelog:
1.2.0

  • A builder on the “Blocks” screen. Choose a block and its options and read off the finished shortcode and the finished block code side by side, with a live preview of the real block next to them. For everyone who works with the Classic Editor, Elementor, WPBakery or Divi and never sees the block settings of the editor.
  • Every form of every block can be put together there, not only the six defaults – the “Form” list holds all 31 building blocks that belong on a page.
  • Only the options the chosen block actually has are shown: a seal is never offered a review count, and a carousel never a review ID. The rule comes from the same catalogue the block editor follows, so the two cannot drift apart.
  • Source (whole account, one location, one review group), number, from-stars, platforms, product, look, circle colour and language – all of it ends up in the shortcode, correctly quoted.
  • “Set up” on each of the six block cards jumps into the builder with that block chosen.
  • “Create a page with this block” starts a draft page with exactly what was put together, instead of always the score badge.
  • “Blocks” now also names the three placements that are not blocks – top bar, footer bar and the tab at the edge of the screen – with a drawing, their on/off state and a link to their settings. The settings link back for everything that is a block.
  • German: the block settings panel “Display” is now “Anzeige” instead of a second “Darstellung”.

1.1.0

  • The tab at the edge of the screen can now be switched on for the whole website, like the two bars. It floats above every page and opens summary and reviews without leaving it.
  • The three site-wide placements have their own settings card with a drawing of where each one sits – instead of two checkboxes between the appearance settings.
  • Look, source (whole account, one location or one review group) and, for the tab, the number of reviews can now be set per placement.
  • The reputify_site_bar filter also receives 'tab' now, next to 'top' and 'bottom'.

1.0.0

  • First public release.
